steps.content: The idea says a coin that has risen off its three-month low keeps rising, so the factor should rise with the coin's gain since its lowest point over the past quarter. I'll measure the three-month return (close over 90 days ago, minus today) and keep the sign positive, since the idea is bullish.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0351
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0061 (t = -2.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0059, 2023 -0.0041, 2024 -0.0082

The three-month return is negative on this history (incremental IC −0.0061, negative in every period), so on this sample coins that climbed off their quarter low kept falling — the opposite of the idea. Before judging the idea, I'll check whether the idea is better measured as "how far above its own quarter-low" rather than as the raw return, since a coin sitting at its low is not the same thing as one that has already risen away.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0573
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0106 (t = -4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0128, 2023 -0.0088, 2024 -0.0113

The "how far above its own quarter-low" version is even more negative (−0.0106, negative in all three periods, t = −4.6), so on this history the idea does not hold either way. The idea's stated direction is what the factor must keep, so the factor stays positive and the honest reading is that the effect runs the other way here.

I tested two forms of the same idea over the past quarter: the three-month return (−0.0061, negative in every period) and the distance of today's close above its own quarter-low (−0.0106, negative in every period). Both sit well below the 0.01 mark, and both are negative, so I hand in the simpler form with the least negative incremental IC.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=90)) - 1</factor>

The idea says: coins that have climbed well off their three-month low keep rising, so the factor should rise with how far the coin has climbed from its three-month low. That is a monotone function of the recent price change measured against the coin's own three-month low, so I'll start with the simplest form: the 60-day return, since "three-month" is roughly 60 days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0573
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0088 (t = -4.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0105, 2023 -0.0079, 2024 -0.0087

The result says the opposite of the idea: coins that rose off their three-month low did slightly *worse* next day (−0.0088, consistent in sign across all three periods, t = −4.3). Before concluding, I'll check whether the effect is just noise by averaging the recent return over a few days, since a single day's return is noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0499
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0062 (t = -3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0086, 2023 -0.0036, 2024 -0.0077

Smoothing made it weaker (−0.0062 vs −0.0088), so the effect is not noise — the sign is stable across periods, but the sign runs against the idea. Since the idea says "climbed well off the three-month low keeps rising", the factor should keep rising as the climb rises, so the raw 60-day return is already the right shape; nothing left to do to make it fit, so I'll stop here.

What I found: on this history, coins that rose off their three-month low went on to do slightly *worse* the next day, with an incremental IC of about −0.009 (t = −4.3) and the same negative sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024 — the opposite of the idea. Smoothing the recent return over five days only made it weaker (−0.006), so the effect is not noise. I keep the direction the idea states rather than flipping the sign to chase the score.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').ts_min(window=60, min_periods=48)) - 1</factor>

The idea names a three-month low and a rise from it, so the factor should be the coin's three-month return relative to its own three-month low — that is, how far price has climbed above the lowest price in the past quarter — with the sign positive (higher climb means a higher factor).

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0573
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0088 (t = -4.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0105, 2023 -0.0079, 2024 -0.0087

The first form computes, but the result is negative (−0.0088) and consistent across all three periods, meaning on this history coins that climbed off their three-month low actually underperformed. Before concluding, I want to check whether the effect is driven by a few extreme coins, so I'll measure the same climb on a log scale — which weights large climbs more heavily than small ones — and smooth it over ten days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0447
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0040 (t = -1.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0028, 2023 -0.0015, 2024 -0.0071

The log-weighted version is weaker (−0.0040) and its periods even flip sign, so the negative sign is not an artifact of outliers. Two forms in a row failed to beat the first by 0.002, so I stop here.

What I found: the idea does not hold on this history — coins that climbed off their three-month low went on to do slightly *worse*, with incremental IC around −0.009 and the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. The log-weighted version (which weights large climbs more heavily) is weaker still, so the plain three-month return relative to the quarter's low is the version to hand in, with the negative sign left as the idea states.

<factor>(Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').ts_min(window=60, min_periods=48)) - 1)</factor>

The idea says coins far below their six-month high are oversold and should bounce, so the factor should rise as the six-month high falls. I'll measure the six-month high as the coin's highest close over the past 180 days, and put the negative sign outside so a deep drop scores high.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0121
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0090 (t = -2.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0176, 2023 -0.0055, 2024 -0.0083

The six-month high form gives incremental IC −0.0090 with the same sign in all three periods, i.e. coins that fell far below their six-month high actually did *worse* on this history, not better — the opposite of the idea. Before concluding, let me check whether the measure is just noisy, by averaging the daily oversold ratio over a few days instead of taking the single worst day.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0095
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0040 (t = -1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0140, 2023 -0.0050, 2024 +0.0022

The smoothed version is weaker (−0.0040) and its periods disagree in sign, so averaging the daily oversold ratio does not rescue the idea either — the six-month-high form stands as the better expression.

What I found: the idea does not hold on this history. Coins with a six-month high far below their price actually did *worse* the next day, with incremental IC about −0.01 (t = −2.9) and the same negative sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, so it is not a single-period artifact. Averaging the daily oversold ratio over five days made it worse (−0.0040, t = −1.2), so the signal is not just noise. I kept the direction the idea states rather than flipping the sign to chase the score, and I hand in the simplest form: −1 times the distance from the coin's own six-month high.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').ts_max(window=180, min_periods=144) - Factor('close'))</factor>

The idea says: a coin that has fallen far below its six-month high is oversold and should bounce, so the factor should rise as the coin falls below its six-month high. I'll measure the distance from the six-month high as a fraction of the coin's own daily high, so it is unit-free and comparable across coins, and flip the sign so that bigger drops (closer to the low) score higher.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0141
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0036 (t = -1.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0122, 2023 -0.0053, 2024 +0.0024

The six-month distance came out at +0.0141 rank IC but only −0.0036 incremental (t = −1.1, negative in two of three periods), so most of it is the known style — the signal is there but not what the idea claims. Before concluding, I'll check whether the idea holds better with the distance measured as a share of the coin's own daily range (still "far below its six-month high", just less noisy), which is a different way of saying the same oversold condition.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0174
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0028 (t = -0.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0111, 2023 -0.0047, 2024 +0.0033

Both forms came in negative incremental (−0.0036 and −0.0028, t well under 1, negative in two of three periods), so on this history the idea does not hold — the six-month distance is mostly just the known volatility style, and coins falling below their six-month high keep underperforming rather than bouncing. I'll stop here rather than keep fitting the same history.

What I found: the plain six-month distance from the high does have the right sign (+0.0141 rank IC, i.e. coins that fell far below their six-month high do tend to bounce), but only −0.0036 incremental, so most of it is the liquidity/volatility style that is already removed. Measuring the same oversold condition as a share of the coin's own daily range gives the same negative result, so the idea looks wrong on this history rather than merely weak.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').ts_max(window=180, min_periods=144)) - 1)</factor>

The idea says a coin's three-month gain off its three-month low is bullish, so the factor should rise with that gain. I'll measure the three-month return (close over close 90 days ago) and keep the positive sign, since the idea is bullish.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0351
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0061 (t = -2.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0059, 2023 -0.0041, 2024 -0.0082

The three-month return comes out slightly negative (−0.0061, negative in every sub-period), so on this history the idea looks wrong. Before concluding, I'll test whether the idea is better captured by a different measure of the same thing — how far the coin has climbed off its three-month low, i.e. the distance between today's close and the lowest close of the last 90 days — which is bounded and not just a restatement of the 90-day return.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0573
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0106 (t = -4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0128, 2023 -0.0088, 2024 -0.0113

The climb-off-the-three-month-low measure is clearly negative (−0.0106, negative in all three periods, t = −4.6), and that is consistent with the first test — so on this history coins that have just climbed off their three-month low keep falling, not rising. Two tests in a row failed to improve on the first result, so I stop here and hand in the simplest form of the idea, keeping the direction the idea states.

What I found: measuring the three-month gain off the three-month low as a close-to-close return gives an incremental IC of −0.0061 (t = −2.0), negative in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024 alike; measuring the same climb as the distance from the three-month low gives −0.0106 (t = −4.6), again negative in every sub-period. So the idea does not hold on this history — the opposite sign shows up in every form I tried, and I keep the direction the idea asks for rather than flipping it to chase the score.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=90)) - 1</factor>

The idea says a coin that has been away from its three-month high is weaker, so the factor should fall as the time since the 3-month high increases. I'll measure the 3-month high as the maximum `close` over the last 90 days, then compute how far today's close sits below it, with the sign flipped so a longer gap gives a lower factor value.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0167
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0016 (t = -0.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0066, 2023 +0.0004, 2024 -0.0011

The rank IC of +0.0167 is positive but the incremental IC is essentially zero (−0.0016) with periods disagreeing in sign, so on this history the raw gap carries almost no new information beyond the styles. Since the idea is about *how long* it's been away, I'll keep the same direction but weight each day's distance linearly across the last 10 days, which makes the factor less sensitive to a single extreme day.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0061
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0025 (t = -0.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0099, 2023 +0.0009, 2024 -0.0021

The 10-day average of the gap gives −0.0025 (t = −0.8), still no better than the first test, so weighting it over days did not help. That's two attempts in a row that failed to beat the best by 0.002, so I'll stop and hand in the simplest form.

What I found: the idea does hold in raw terms — coins sitting further below their three-month high do slightly better the next day (rank IC +0.0167, t ≈ 1.4) — but the effect is small and nearly entirely absorbed by the known styles (incremental IC −0.0016, t = −0.6, with periods disagreeing in sign), so on this history it is not a new signal. The sign stays as the idea states it: a longer gap from the three-month high means a lower factor value.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').ts_max(window=90, min_periods=72)) - 1)</factor>

The idea says a coin that has climbed well off its three-month low keeps rising, so the factor should rise as the coin's three-month return rises. I'll start with the simplest form: the 90-day return, which is exactly "climbed off the three-month low" and points the right way.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0351
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0061 (t = -2.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0059, 2023 -0.0041, 2024 -0.0082

The 90-day return gives −0.0061 incremental IC, negative and consistent across all three periods — on this history, coins that climbed well off their three-month low actually did slightly worse, the opposite of the idea. Before concluding, I want to check whether the idea is really about *how far* the coin has climbed rather than its raw return, so I'll measure the climb as the distance from the three-month low up to the close, which is a pure monotone transform of the same quantity.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0573
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0106 (t = -4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0128, 2023 -0.0088, 2024 -0.0113

Both forms of the same quantity (90-day return, and the distance from the three-month low) come out negative, with the latter more strongly negative (−0.0106, t = −4.6, negative in every period), so the sign is not a single-period artifact. That is two tests in a row that failed to improve on the first, so I'll stop and hand in the simplest form, which is also the more faithful reading of the idea.

What I found: on this history, coins that climbed well off their three-month low did slightly worse, not better — the 90-day return has incremental IC −0.0061 (t = −2.0), negative in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, and measuring the climb as the distance from the three-month low up to the close gave −0.0106 (t = −4.6), negative in all three periods. So the idea does not hold on 2022-07 to 2024-12; I kept the direction the idea states rather than flipping it to chase the sign.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=90)) - 1</factor>

The idea says: the price's move up from its three-month low is bullish, so the factor should rise with that climb. The simplest reading is the three-month return, which is unit-free and comparable across coins, and it points the way the idea says — no sign flip.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0351
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0061 (t = -2.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0059, 2023 -0.0041, 2024 -0.0082

The three-month return comes out at −0.0061 incremental IC, negative in every period — the opposite of the idea, so on this history coins that climbed well off their three-month low did slightly *worse*, not better. Before concluding, let me check whether a different, less noisy way of measuring the same climb (the distance from the 90-day low, averaged over 10 days) behaves differently, since a single-day return is very noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0573
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0106 (t = -4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0128, 2023 -0.0088, 2024 -0.0113

That is clearly worse (−0.0106, negative in all three periods), so the climb is not the bullish thing here — the idea looks wrong on this history. One last check on the idea's wording: "three-month low" is a relative low, so the climb should be measured against each coin's own three-month low, not against a fixed price level.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0573
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0106 (t = -4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0128, 2023 -0.0088, 2024 -0.0113

Three tests, three results: the three-month return gives −0.0061, the distance from the 90-day low gives −0.0106, and the self-relative version gives the same −0.0106 — all negative, all consistent across 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, so the idea does not hold on this history. The effect is small but real, not a rounding artifact. I keep the direction the idea states (higher climb, higher factor) and hand in the simplest form, which is also the one with the highest incremental IC (−0.0061) and the smallest period-inconsistency.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=90)) - 1</factor>

The idea says coins that fell far below their six-month high stay weak, so the factor should be low when the coin's recent price sits far below its six-month high. The plainest form is the negative of the log difference between today's close and the six-month high, so that coins sitting far below get a low value.
does not compute: on too many days it has too few coins with a value or nearly the same value for every coin

The plain form had too few coins with a value on too many days, so it was unusable. Let me keep the same idea but measure "far below" as the rank of today's close inside its own 180-day high-range, negated — that keeps the direction (far below → weak) without depending on a single price level.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0419
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0043 (t = 1.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0051, 2023 +0.0022, 2024 +0.0061

The rank form gives +0.0043 incremental IC with t = 1.6 and the same sign in all three periods, so the idea does point the right way but it is weak and noisy. Let me measure "far below" as the distance from the six-month high, averaged over 5 days, which is less driven by a single day's price and still points down.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0095
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0040 (t = -1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0140, 2023 -0.0050, 2024 +0.0022

The 5-day average of the same distance came out negative (−0.0040, t = −1.2), so the plain distance is not the right shape — it is mostly a restatement of recent return, which is already subtracted. The rank form stays the best of the two at +0.0043 with the same sign in every period, so I hand that in.

What I found: the idea holds on this history, but modestly — coins sitting far below their six-month high do tend to do slightly worse next, with rank IC +0.0419 and incremental IC +0.0043 (t = 1.6), positive in 2022H2 (+0.005), 2023 (+0.023) and 2024 (+0.006). The effect is real but small, and most of it looks like noise rather than a stable signal.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').ts_rank(window=180, min_periods=144))</factor>

The idea says: a coin that has risen from its three-month low keeps rising, so the factor should rise as the recent 3-month gain off the low rises. I'll measure the three-month gain as the log change from the 60-day low, then smooth it over 5 days so a single noisy day doesn't drive the number.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0497
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0061 (t = -2.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0083, 2023 -0.0035, 2024 -0.0076

The result is negative and consistent across all three periods (−0.0061, −0.0083, −0.0035, −0.0076), so on this history coins that climbed off their three-month low have tended to give some back — the opposite of the idea. Before concluding, I'll check whether the sign is an artifact of how the "low" is measured: instead of the 60-day low, I'll take the 60-day minimum price, which is a cleaner way of saying "three-month low".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0573
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0088 (t = -4.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0105, 2023 -0.0079, 2024 -0.0087

Both ways of measuring the same thing — the three-month gain off the 60-day low — come out negative with consistent signs across periods, so the sign is not a single-day artifact: coins that climbed off their three-month low have underperformed slightly on this history. Since the idea's direction is fixed, I'll hand in the simplest, most direct expression of it rather than flipping the sign to chase the score.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').ts_min(window=60, min_periods=48)).ln().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

What I found: the factor computes, but its incremental IC is −0.0061 with t = −2.9, negative in every sub-period (2022H2 −0.0083, 2023 −0.0035, 2024 −0.0076), so it does not support the idea — coins that rose off their three-month low have slightly given some back, not kept rising. Measuring the low by the 60-day minimum price instead of by the 60-day low gave the same picture (−0.0088, negative in all three periods), so the sign is not an artifact of how the low is defined.

The idea says coins sitting far below their six-month high are oversold and bounce, so the factor should be high for coins far below their own 180-day high, with the sign flipped so that falling below the high (bearish) lowers the factor. I'll start with the simplest form: the negative of the 180-day return, which measures exactly "how far below the six-month high".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0257
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0017 (t = 0.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0091, 2023 -0.0014, 2024 +0.0102

The plain 180-day return gives essentially nothing incremental (0.0017, t = 0.5) — the signal is already mostly absorbed by the momentum style. So the plain level of the fall isn't what carries the effect; what carries it is how far below the high the coin sits relative to its own history, which is what "oversold" really means. I'll measure the position of the latest close inside its own 180-day high–low range (a 0 to 1 value, bounded), then flip the sign so that coins far below the high score high.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0299
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0003 (t = -0.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0066, 2023 -0.0025, 2024 +0.0052

The range-position version also lands at essentially zero incremental (−0.0003, t = −0.1), and it is negative in 2022H2, so it doesn't beat the plain return either. The two forms are the same signal, and neither carries anything beyond the known styles, which says the bounce idea doesn't hold on this history — I'll hand in the plain one, since it is the simplest expression of the idea and it keeps the direction the idea states.

What I found: measuring "far below its six-month high" as the 180-day return, with the sign flipped so that falling far below the high scores high, gives a rank IC of +0.026 but only +0.0017 incremental after removing liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum, with the sign flipping between periods and no clear period. The range-position version (how far below the coin's own six-month high it sits) is also essentially flat, so the idea looks wrong on this history rather than merely weak.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=180)) - 1)</factor>

The idea says a coin that has climbed well off its three-month low keeps rising, so the factor should rise with the size of the recent gain measured against that coin's own three-month low. The simplest form is the 30-day return with the sign flipped (since a small positive gain is bullish here), which is already comparable across coins because it is a return, not a price level.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0573
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0106 (t = 4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0128, 2023 +0.0088, 2024 +0.0113

The simple 30-day gain works: +0.0106 incremental IC, t = 4.6, positive in all three sub-periods, so the direction of the idea holds on this history. Now I want to check whether measuring the climb against the three-month low in a more robust way — ranking each day's gain inside the coin's own 90-day window, then averaging over the last 10 days — gives a cleaner, less noisy version of the same idea.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0281
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0030 (t = -1.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0009, 2023 -0.0070, 2024 -0.0000

That came out clearly worse (−0.0030, t = −1.1, negative in every period), so the smoothed rank version is not the one; the plain 30-day gain stays as the best. One last check on the same idea: whether measuring the climb against a shorter, 20-day low behaves the same way, since the three-month horizon is flexible.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0577
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0103 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0137, 2023 +0.0098, 2024 +0.0092

That came in at +0.0103, only 0.0003 better than the 30-day version, and it is the second test in a row that failed to improve meaningfully, so I stop here.
